title: 静かな通路とにぎやかな広場
paragraphs: A town museum wanted to welcome families without disturbing visitors who preferred silence. Staff initially considered asking all children to speak quietly everywhere. A guide pointed out that this might make families feel unwanted and prevent useful questions. The problem was not simply noise, but the absence of clear expectations in different spaces.
博物館は家族を歓迎し静けさも守りたかった。一律に子どもを静かにさせると歓迎されないと感じ質問も妨げるとガイドが指摘した。空間ごとの期待の不明確さが問題だった。

The museum therefore introduced a lively discovery room near the entrance. Visitors could handle copies of objects and discuss what they noticed. The upstairs gallery remained a quiet space for reading and close observation. [1] separating the activities completely, staff connected them through a trail of short questions. Families could explore an object downstairs before looking for its original upstairs.
入口に複製を触って話せる部屋、上階に静かな鑑賞室を設けた。完全に分けるのでなく短い問いの道筋で結び、下で探究して上で本物を探せた。

The arrangement did not satisfy everyone immediately. Signs were revised after visitors misunderstood one symbol, and guides explained the purpose of each area. Over time, complaints became less frequent. The museum had not chosen between conversation and silence; it had designed opportunities for both, while helping people understand when their behavior affected others. Staff continued asking for feedback rather than assuming the first layout was final.
すぐ全員満足とはならず、誤解された記号を直し目的を説明した。次第に苦情が減り、会話か沈黙かを選ぶのでなく両方の機会を作り他者への影響を伝えた。最初の配置を完成とせず意見を集め続けた。
questions: 完全分離でなく接続する対比。
原因を表す句ではない。
分離も加えたわけではない。
直後に動名詞が続くこの文に不適切。
静かに読んで観察する
a quiet space for reading and close observation
案内を直し意見を集めた
syntax: The problem was not simply noise, but the absence of clear expectations in different spaces.
not simply noise, but the absence of clear expectations in different spaces
問題は単なる音でなく空間ごとの明確な期待がないことだった。
not A but Bで焦点をAからBへ移す。absence ofは〜の不在。

title: 試作品を試す相手
paragraphs: Maya's team designed a phone holder for bicycles as a classroom project. They asked their friends to test it, and everyone said it looked attractive. The team was ready to present the design as a success. Their teacher asked whether the testers had actually used it while wearing gloves or riding over an uneven surface. None had.
マヤ班の自転車用スマホホルダーは友人に外観を褒められ成功と発表しかけたが、手袋や凸凹道で試した人はいなかった。

During a second trial, several cyclists found the small release button difficult to press. The holder stayed secure, [1] removing the phone required more effort than expected. One tester also asked how easily the parts could be replaced if they broke. These questions had not appeared in the team's original survey about appearance.
二度目の試験で小さい解除ボタンを押しにくいと判明した。固定は安全でも取り外しは予想より大変で、破損部品の交換も質問された。外観調査にはない問いだった。

Maya changed the button shape and added a simple diagram showing how the pieces fitted together. The final presentation included the first design and the problems discovered later. She explained that praise from familiar people could be encouraging without being sufficient evidence of practical success. Choosing testers whose actual circumstances differed from the designers' own had helped the team ask better questions before claiming that its product was ready.
ボタン形状と組立図を改善し初案と問題も発表した。知人の称賛は励みでも実用成功の十分な証拠ではなく、設計者と状況の違う試験者が完成宣言前のよい問いを助けたと説明した。
questions: 固定の良さと外しにくさを対比。
外しにくさは固定の理由と述べない。
結果として単純接続しない。
removing the phone required more effort
友人は見た目を評価した。
異なる立場の試験者の利点は？
設計者が見落とす問いが出る
実使用条件が問題を発見。
syntax: 誰もそうしていなかった。
直前のhad actually used以下を省略して繰り返しを避ける。Noneは試した人がゼロの意味。

title: 農場へ届く食堂の記録
paragraphs: A college cafeteria bought vegetables from a nearby farm. Every week, the kitchen ordered the same amount, even though student attendance changed with exams and holidays. Sometimes vegetables remained unused, while on other days the cook had to buy extra from another supplier. The farmer could not easily adjust because she received only a final order number.
大学食堂は試験や休暇で人数が変わっても近くの農家へ毎週同量を頼み、余りや買い足しが起きた。農家には最終数しか届かず調整しにくかった。

The kitchen began sharing a simple calendar of expected events and a weekly record of actual use. The farmer did not need private information about individual students. She needed a clearer picture of when demand might rise or fall. [1] the numbers were still uncertain, the earlier information allowed her to discuss possible changes before vegetables were packed.
行事予測カレンダーと実使用週記録を共有した。個々の学生の私情報でなく需要変化が必要だった。数値は不確実でも早期情報で梱包前に変更を相談できた。

After a term, both sides reported fewer last-minute surprises. The system did not eliminate weather problems or make every prediction correct. It improved the conversation between people whose work was already connected. Students studying the project noticed that reducing waste was not only a matter of telling consumers to finish their meals; it could also involve changing how organizations exchanged information before food reached a plate.
学期後、双方の直前の驚きが減った。天候問題や予測誤りをなくしたのでなく、既につながる仕事の対話を改善した。無駄削減は完食の呼びかけだけでなく、皿に届く前の組織間情報の交換にも関わると学生は気づいた。
questions: 不確実さが残るのに有効という譲歩。
農家が必要とした情報は？
需要が増減しそうな時期
when demand might rise or fall
天候問題や予測誤りは残る
syntax: It improved the conversation between people whose work was already connected.
between people whose work was already connected
既につながる仕事をする人々の対話を改善した。
whose workはpeopleを説明する所有格関係詞。between以下はconversationを具体化する。

title: 勧められなかった一冊
paragraphs: An online bookshop recommended novels to customers based on their previous purchases. Haru liked the service because it quickly found stories similar to those she already enjoyed. After several months, however, she noticed that nearly every recommendation belonged to the same genre. Books outside that category rarely appeared on her screen.
書店の履歴推薦でハルは好みに似た小説を素早く得たが、同ジャンルばかりと気づいた。

At a town book club, another member lent her a collection of travel essays. Haru had not expected to enjoy it, but one essay made her reconsider a place she had visited. She realized that a useful recommendation system might still narrow what she encountered. It could recognize a pattern in her choices without knowing every interest she might develop.
読書会で借りた旅行随筆は予想外に面白く、訪問地を考え直した。推薦は既存の傾向を見ても将来の関心を全て知るわけでなく、出会いを狭めうる。

Haru continued using the shop's suggestions. [1], she began choosing one unfamiliar book each month from a librarian's display. Some disappointed her, while others opened new questions. She did not treat the two methods as enemies. One helped her find likely favorites efficiently; the other created chances for surprise. Her reading became broader when she decided how to use the recommendations rather than accepting them as a complete picture of her taste.
推薦と並行して司書展示から毎月未知の本を選んだ。外れも新しい問いもあり、効率と驚きの二方法を敵視しなかった。推薦を好みの全体像とせず使い方を決めて読書が広がった。
questions: 理由を一つに限定しない。
前文の言換えではない。
将来の関心を全ては分からない
未開拓の関心を捉えきれない。
did not treat the two methods as enemies
syntax: It could recognize a pattern in her choices without knowing every interest she might develop.
without knowing every interest she might develop
選択の傾向は認識できても将来の関心を全て知るわけではなかった。
interestの後に関係代名詞の省略された修飾節が続く。

title: 橋の名前を決める前に
paragraphs: A newly built footbridge needed a name. The town invited residents to suggest one and planned to choose the most popular entry through an online vote. Within a day, a humorous suggestion had spread widely beyond the town. Thousands of votes arrived from people who had never crossed the bridge.
歩道橋の名のオンライン投票で冗談案が町外へ広まり何千票も入った。

Some residents enjoyed the joke, while others wanted a name connected with local history. The council recognized that it had not explained who the vote was intended to represent or whether the result would be binding. Simply rejecting an unpopular result after seeing it would also damage trust.
楽しむ人と地元史の名を望む人がおり、誰の声を代表し結果に拘束力があるか未説明と気づいた。結果を見てから拒むのも信頼を傷つける。

The council paused the process and publicly described the problem. It held an open meeting before announcing a new procedure for future naming projects. [1] a vote was used again, the purpose, eligibility rules, and role of the result would be stated in advance. For the present bridge, the council invited representatives of different local groups to discuss a shortlist. Residents did not all agree with the outcome, but they could see the reasoning and the limits of the revised decision.
中断理由を公開し会議後、今後もし投票するなら目的、資格、結果の役割を先に示すとした。今回は各団体代表が候補を協議。全員一致ではないが改訂判断の理由と限界が見えた。
questions: 再利用する場合の条件。
節へ直接接続できない。
当初不明だったことは？
投票が誰を代表し結果に拘束力があるか
インターネットの発明者
whether the result would be binding
改訂後も残ったことは？
透明でも全員一致とは限らない。
did not all agree with the outcome
syntax: Simply rejecting an unpopular result after seeing it would also damage trust.
Simply rejecting an unpopular result after seeing it
結果を見てから不人気な結果を拒むだけでも信頼を傷つける。
動名詞句が主語。wouldは想定上の結果を示す。

title: 昼寝する猫と調査の条件
paragraphs: A student photographer wanted to know which corners of her house her cat preferred. She photographed the cat every afternoon and marked its position on a floor plan. After a week, the sunny sofa appeared to be the clear favorite. She wrote that the cat preferred soft furniture to every other place.
猫の好きな場所を調べる学生は毎午後撮影し図面へ記録。一週で日なたのソファが最多で、柔らかい家具を何より好むと書いた。

Her brother asked whether the afternoon was representative of the entire day. Early in the morning, the cat often sat near the kitchen, and at night it slept upstairs. The photographer had chosen an observation time that favored one part of the animal's routine. Her records were accurate descriptions of those afternoons, [1] they were not a complete account of the cat's preferences.
兄は午後が全日を代表するか尋ね、朝は台所、夜は上階と指摘。午後の記録は正確でも全好みではなかった。

She changed her question to ask where the cat rested during the afternoon and clearly stated the observation period. For a broader project, she would need records at other times as well. The experience taught her that improving a claim did not always require collecting more data immediately. Sometimes the first step was to make the question and conclusion fit the evidence she already had.
問いを午後の休憩場所へ限定し観察期間を明記した。広い調査なら他時刻も必要。常に即追加データでなく、まず問いと結論を今の証拠に合わせる改善もあると学んだ。
questions: 正確な限定記録と不完全な全体像の対比。
最初に改善したものは？
証拠の範囲に限定した。
make the question and conclusion fit the evidence
syntax: Her records were accurate descriptions of those afternoons
記録はそれらの午後の正確な記述だった。
butに先行する節。accurateはdescriptionsを修飾する。

title: 長く使う制服の交換会
paragraphs: A school organized a uniform exchange so families could pass on clothes that no longer fitted. Volunteers sorted donations by size and placed them on tables. The first event attracted many visitors, but some families left without taking anything. Organizers assumed that the available sizes had not matched their needs.
サイズ別の制服交換会に人は来たが持ち帰らない家庭があり、主催者はサイズ不一致と思った。

An anonymous questionnaire revealed another concern. Some visitors had felt uncomfortable choosing clothes while classmates watched. Others did not know whether taking a uniform meant they were admitting financial difficulty. The organizers had described the event only as support for families with limited money. [1], they had unintentionally made participation feel like a public statement about income.
匿名調査では同級生の視線や困窮の公表に感じる不安が分かった。金銭支援だけと説明した結果、参加が所得についての声明になっていた。

For the next exchange, they emphasized keeping useful clothing in circulation and welcomed all families. They also offered appointments for anyone who preferred a quieter visit. Donations and collections were arranged separately, so giving was not a condition of receiving. More uniforms found new owners. The organizers learned that a service could remove a practical barrier while creating a social one if the way it was described made people worry about how others would judge them.
次回は資源循環を強調し全家庭を歓迎、静かな予約枠を設け、寄付と受領を分け寄付を条件にしなかった。再使用が増え、実用の障壁を消しても説明が他者評価の不安という社会的障壁を生みうると学んだ。
questions: 金銭支援だけの説明による結果。
原因が説明されている。
調査で分かった不安は？
他人から経済状態を判断される
寄付のサイズが全て同じ
新品しか受け取れない
参加の社会的意味への不安。
寄付しなくても受け取れる
giving was not a condition of receiving
syntax: The first event attracted many visitors, but some families left without taking anything.
some families left without taking anything
初回は多くの人を集めたが何も受け取らず帰る家庭もあった。
butで集客と利用の差を示す。without takingは受領せずに。

title: 録音された方言の持ち主
paragraphs: A language club recorded conversations with older residents to create a local dialect collection. Students carefully asked permission before each interview. They thought this agreement meant they could use every part of the recording in any future project. Their adviser asked them to read the actual consent form again.
言語部は方言記録で毎回許可を得たため、全録音を将来のどんな企画にも使えると思ったが顧問が同意書を再読させた。

The form allowed recordings to be played at a school exhibition. It did not mention posting complete conversations on the internet. One resident was happy to share a story with local students but did not want a family disagreement to become searchable online. The club realized that agreeing to one use was not necessarily agreeing to every possible use.
学校展示での再生のみでネット全公開はなく、地域学生へは話しても家族の口論の検索公開は望まない人もいた。一用途の同意は全用途とは違った。

They contacted each speaker before preparing the website. [1] permission was clear, they kept the recording offline. Some speakers approved short edited sections, while others chose written summaries. The website therefore contained fewer audio clips than the students had expected. However, the process strengthened their relationship with the people whose voices they were preserving. They learned that collecting valuable material also created responsibilities toward the people who had trusted them with it.
サイト前に再確認し、許可が明確になるまでは非公開。短い編集音声を認める人も文章要約を選ぶ人もいて音声数は減ったが関係は強まった。大切な資料の収集は声を託した人への責任も生むと学んだ。
questions: 許可が明確になるまで公開しない。
明確だから非公開ではない。
毎回明確な時に非公開という意味は合わない。
当初許可されていた用途は？
音声数は減ったが関係は強まった
全住民との関係を断絶
量だけで評価しない結論。
syntax: The club realized that agreeing to one use was not necessarily agreeing to every possible use.
agreeing to one use was not necessarily agreeing to every possible use
一用途への同意が必ずしも全用途への同意ではないと部は気づいた。
not necessarilyは必ずしも〜ではないという部分否定。

title: 節電の掲示と本当の変化
paragraphs: An office displayed signs reminding employees to switch off unused lights. At the end of the month, its electricity bill was lower. The manager wanted to announce that the signs had saved a large amount of energy. A colleague suggested checking whether anything else had changed during the same period.
節電札を出した月に電気代が下がり、管理者は大幅節電と発表したかった。同僚が他の変化も確認した。

Several employees had been away on a training course, and the weather had been cooler than usual. Both factors could have reduced electricity use independently of the signs. The lower bill was real, but the reason for it was not yet certain. [1] measuring the number of lights left on after work, the office could gather evidence more directly connected with the message.
研修での不在と涼しい天候も独立に減らしうる。請求減は事実でも理由は不確かで、終業後の点灯数を測れば札に直接関わる証拠になる。

For the following weeks, staff recorded empty rooms with lights still on at a fixed time. They also noted holidays and other unusual conditions. The new records suggested an improvement, although they did not separate every possible influence. The manager reported the result cautiously. She kept the signs because they were simple and useful, while avoiding a precise claim that the available information could not justify.
数週間、定時の無人室点灯と休日などを記録した。改善は示唆されても全要因を分離できず慎重に報告。札は簡便で有用だから残すが、情報で正当化できない厳密な数値主張は避けた。
questions: 測定することで、という方法。
後ろは動名詞で条件節ではない。
研修不在と涼しい天候
同時期の変化として挙げる。
the weather had been cooler than usual
改善を慎重に述べ厳密な断定を避けた
全効果を札だけに断定
証拠の限界を踏まえた。
syntax: 請求額の減少は事実だったが理由はまだ確かでなかった。
観測事実と原因の推定をbutで区別する。itは請求額の減少を受ける。

title: 校庭の木を数える方法
paragraphs: A school environment group decided to record the trees on its grounds. Members counted every trunk and prepared a colorful total for the website. Their teacher asked what the number would help readers understand. A hundred young trees and a hundred mature trees did not necessarily provide the same kind of shade or habitat.
環境班が校内の幹を全て数えカラフルな総数を作ると、先生は何の理解を助けるか尋ねた。若木百本と成木百本で日陰や生息環境は同じとは限らない。

The group added information about size, location, and visible condition. They photographed each tree from a marked point so future students could compare changes. [1] the project required more work than a simple count, it created a record that could answer more useful questions later. A local gardener helped them describe what they could observe without guessing at hidden problems.
大きさ、位置、見える状態を加え固定地点から撮影した。手間は増えても将来有用な問いに答えられる記録になった。園芸家は見えない問題を推測せず観察可能な記述を助けた。

The final display still included a total, but did not treat that figure as a complete measure of environmental value. Students explained why a variety of observations was needed. They also left instructions for updating the map each spring. Their aim had shifted from producing an impressive number to building information that another group could maintain and use, even after the original members had left school.
総数も残すが環境価値の全尺度とはせず多様な観察の理由と春の更新方法を示した。立派な数から、卒業後も他班が維持利用できる情報へ目的が変わった。
questions: 手間増にもかかわらず価値がある譲歩。
後ろの完全節を取れない。
前置詞で節を取れない。
required more work than a simple count
固定地点の写真の目的は？
幹を数えないためだけ
記録の再現性を高める。
見えない問題を推測しない。
印象的な総数から継続利用できる情報へ
維持と利用を重視した。
another group could maintain and use
syntax: Their aim had shifted from producing an impressive number to building information that another group could maintain and use
to building information that another group could maintain and use
目標は立派な数を出すことから他班も維持利用できる情報を作ることへ移った。
from A to BのA・Bは動名詞句。thatはinformationを修飾する。
